highlights.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
highlights.summary: Answer‑distribution trajectories are a stochastic‑dynamics representation that tracks a model’s full predictive distribution over answers throughout the reasoning process, offering a finer view than endpoint accuracy or entropy profiles.
highlights.detail: Entropy profiles capture uncertainty but not the competing hypotheses behind it. Answer‑distribution trajectories record the entire answer distribution at each reasoning step, revealing how hypotheses rise and fall. This enables classification of reasoning phases such as exploration, revision, motion, and commitment. Researchers can now distinguish distinct dynamical mechanisms underlying LLM reasoning.

highlights.title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?
highlights.summary: A controlled human study of six reasoning formats shows a mismatch: participants prefer planning‑ and decomposition‑based representations, yet those formats provide less support for evaluating LLM outputs.
highlights.detail: The study randomized task domains, problem instances, and representation order via a web framework. Participants judged structural understanding, error detection, localization, and trust calibration across tasks of varying complexity. Six reasoning formats were compared, revealing that perceived preference does not align with actual evaluation assistance. Findings suggest design of explanation interfaces should prioritize utility over user preference.

highlights.title: PlannerForge: LLM Agents for Scenario-Based Testing of Motion Planners in Autonomous Driving
highlights.summary: PlannerForge is an LLM‑agent framework that unifies all stages of scenario‑based testing for autonomous driving, from generation to assessment, and was evaluated with ten off‑the‑shelf LLMs.
highlights.detail: Traditional testing pipelines treat scenario generation, retrieval, modification, execution, and analysis as separate tools. PlannerForge adds LLM‑enhanced ADS enhancement and benchmarking stages, creating a single coordinated workflow. Evaluation covered tasks such as scenario generation, selection, and result analysis across the ten models. The results demonstrate that LLM agents can handle the full testing lifecycle, reducing integration overhead.

highlights.title: Show HN: LLM Attention Visualization
highlights.summary: A Hacker News post shares a tool that visualizes attention weights in large language models, letting users explore token‑level influence.
highlights.detail: The visualization renders attention matrices across transformer layers, highlighting which input tokens affect specific output tokens. Users can interactively select layers and heads to inspect model focus. Such insight aids debugging and understanding of model behavior without modifying the underlying model code.

highlights.title: Generalized DBLog: A Verified Contract for Interleaving Database Rows with a Change Log
highlights.summary: Netflix’s DBLog algorithm interleaves chunked table reads with live change logs, using watermarks to ensure copied rows never overwrite newer updates, and has been adopted by Debezium and Flink CDC.
highlights.detail: DBLog reads database tables in segments while simultaneously ingesting the live change‑data‑capture stream. Watermarks mark the latest log entry seen for each segment, guaranteeing that stale copied rows are superseded by newer log updates. Formal verification proved that the interleaved output reconstructs the source state exactly, and the design has been incorporated into popular CDC frameworks.

items.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
items.summary: AlphaGenome Atlas maps the molecular effects of nine billion single‑letter DNA variants across the human genome.
items.detail: The atlas predicts how each possible single‑nucleotide change influences molecular phenotypes, enabling systematic assessment of variant pathogenicity. It leverages DeepMind’s protein‑structure models to infer functional impact. Researchers can query any genomic position to retrieve predicted effects, supporting precision‑medicine studies and variant prioritization pipelines.

items.title: How GPT-5.6 Sol helps run quantum computing experiments
items.summary: An MIT researcher uses GPT‑5.6 Sol with Codex to autonomously run quantum computing experiments, analyze results, and calibrate qubits.
items.detail: The workflow combines GPT‑5.6 Sol for high‑level experiment design with Codex for generating low‑level control code. The system iteratively runs experiments on quantum hardware, processes measurement data, and adjusts qubit parameters to improve fidelity. This demonstrates a fully AI‑driven loop from hypothesis to hardware tuning in quantum research.

items.title: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5
items.summary: ChatGPT Images 2.5 converts ideas, sketches, and reference photos into personalized, polished images that better reflect user concepts.
items.detail: Version 2.5 adds support for user‑provided sketches and reference images, improving prompt‑to‑image alignment. The model produces higher‑resolution outputs with refined textures, reducing the need for post‑processing. It aims to capture nuanced visual intent while maintaining the speed of the ChatGPT interface.

items.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
items.summary: An AI‑generated solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem is released, including a write‑up and a formal Lean proof.
items.detail: The solution comprises a detailed mathematical exposition and a machine‑checked proof encoded in the Lean theorem prover. It represents a novel attempt at using AI to tackle one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven unsolved problems. The authors provide both the narrative and the formal code for community verification.

items.title: Safety for Whom? Refusing the Right Subset of a Topic, Not the Whole Topic
items.summary: A Hugging Face blog post argues that safety mechanisms should block specific harmful subtopics rather than banning entire topics.
items.detail: The article critiques blanket content bans, suggesting they over‑restrict benign discourse. It proposes a granular approach that identifies and filters only the dangerous subsets within broader subjects. This perspective informs future policy design for AI moderation tools and community guidelines.

items.title: Model: IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B
items.summary: The HF model IFM/K2‑Horizon‑MoVA‑36B‑A4B has recorded 3,205 downloads and 237 likes on the platform.
items.detail: The model is a 36‑billion‑parameter text generation system hosted on Hugging Face’s Model Hub. Since its release it has attracted a modest community following, as reflected in the download and like counts. Users can integrate it via the standard Transformers API for various generation tasks.

items.title: Security updates for Tuesday
items.summary: Security updates were released Tuesday for AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Red Hat, and SUSE, covering numerous packages across each distribution.
items.detail: The patches address vulnerabilities in libraries such as expat, git-lfs, strongswan, and kernel‑rt, among others. Each distro distributes the updates through its package manager to ensure system integrity. Administrators are advised to apply the updates promptly to mitigate potential exploits.

items.title: Jellyfin 12.0 released
items.summary: Jellyfin 12.0 was released, featuring database performance improvements, an upgrade to FFmpeg 8.1, and enhanced handling of book and comic media.
items.detail: The new version optimizes database queries, resulting in faster media library indexing. Upgrading to FFmpeg 8.1 expands codec support and improves transcoding efficiency. Additional parsing logic refines metadata extraction for books and comics, offering a smoother user experience in both the web client and server.

items.title: [$] Stabilizing Rust's never type
items.summary: Rust’s never type (`!`) was stabilized on August 24 2024 after over two years of work, making the previously unstable feature officially part of the language.
items.detail: The never type marks functions that never return, such as those that always panic or loop forever. Stabilizing it required a small breaking change to earlier Rust editions, which maintainers verified would affect minimal real‑world code. The change enables developers to write more precise type signatures without relying on unstable compiler internals.

items.title: Anti-Doomscroll Tamagotchi Only Lives if You Do
items.summary: Hackaday reports a Tamagotchi‑style device that stops functioning unless the user remains active, aiming to curb doom‑scrolling by tying its life to the owner’s engagement.
items.detail: The gadget monitors user interaction and will ‘die’ if the owner spends too much time passively scrolling. It encourages periodic breaks by requiring the user to perform simple tasks to keep the virtual pet alive. The design leverages behavioral nudges rather than technical restrictions.

items.title: Are Desktop PC-ABS Prints Outperformed by Industrial FDM? Not Really
items.summary: A test comparing desktop PC‑ABS prints to industrial FDM parts found no significant performance advantage for the industrial machine.
items.detail: The experiment printed identical geometries using PC‑ABS filament on a consumer‑grade printer and an industrial‑grade FDM system. Dimensional accuracy, tensile strength, and surface finish were measured and showed overlapping tolerances. The results suggest that material properties dominate over printer class for this filament.

items.title: Disassembling a Mini Air Blower to Make RC Airplanes
items.summary: A YouTube maker disassembles a compact air blower to repurpose its motor for powering RC airplane propellers, offering a lightweight alternative to compressors.
items.detail: The mini blower’s high‑rpm motor is extracted and coupled to a custom propeller hub, providing steady airflow without the bulk of a traditional compressor. The conversion retains the blower’s built‑in speed controller, allowing fine‑tuned thrust control. Flight tests demonstrated comparable lift to small electric fans while reducing overall weight.

items.title: OntoKG-EQ: A provenance-grounded, competency-question-governed knowledge graph for auditable analyst querying
items.summary: OntoKG‑EQ introduces a provenance‑grounded knowledge graph for equity analysts, linking every metric to one of five predefined competency questions to ensure reproducible, auditable queries.
items.detail: The system couples a core ontology, governed by competency questions, with a provenance‑aware graph where each class, property, and metric cites its originating question. Market data is materialized into the graph, then validated against declarative shape constraints. Queries are expressed as graph traversals that directly map to the competency questions, providing traceable answers for analysts.

items.title: SemBridge: Compiling Consumer Observations into Cross-Stack Communication Plans
items.summary: SemBridge generates typed contracts for cross‑runtime tensor communication, handling 72 structural transitions, confirming 54 complete obligations, and rejecting 40 invalid candidate plans.
items.detail: SemBridge compiles runtime and graph facts into a contract describing the consumer‑visible result and delivery obligations. A deterministic lowerer produces backend‑neutral communication plans, while a symbolic checker validates each plan before execution across CUDA/NCCL and CANN/HCCL. The layout‑only planner explores all structural transitions, but only a subset meet the full obligation set, and the minimizer discards semantically invalid options.

items.title: Transversal Fanout for Fault Tolerant Distributed Quantum Computing: Analysis and Application
items.summary: The paper proposes using transversal logical operations on encoded quantum blocks to implement distributed fanout with fewer non‑local gates, demonstrated on Bivariate Bicycle code blocks.
items.detail: Logical fanout spreads a control qubit’s state to many remote targets, traditionally requiring many inter‑node CNOTs. By exploiting transversal operations inherent to the error‑correcting code, the authors construct fanout circuits that replace many non‑local gates with local transversal ones. The approach is illustrated using BB‑code blocks, showing reduced communication overhead while preserving logical correctness.

items.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
items.summary: A measurement study compares self‑hosted LLM inference on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin and a near‑edge server, finding GPU‑enabled servers achieve lowest latency while the Jetson consumes less energy per token.
items.detail: The authors benchmarked several open‑weight LLMs and quantization schemes using a fixed question‑answer workload. Metrics collected include per‑token decoding latency, prefill latency, model footprint, accuracy against GPT‑4o, and total energy consumption. Results show the server’s GPU mode minimizes compute‑side latency, whereas the Jetson’s ARM‑based GPU delivers the lowest measured energy per token, highlighting trade‑offs for edge deployments.

items.title: Exploring the Genesis Platform Capabilities to Accelerate Scientific Discovery in OPAL
items.summary: The DOE Genesis platform enabled a 40‑day plant phenotyping campaign across Oak Ridge and Frontier, automating model distribution and provenance for cross‑facility experiments.
items.detail: Genesis provides managed execution, versioned model distribution, and governed LLM access across remote compute sites. In the campaign, phenotyping data from the Advanced Plant Phenotyping Laboratory were streamed to the Frontier supercomputer for analysis. The workflow automated data provenance, reducing manual integration effort and accelerating scientific insight generation.

items.title: lostb1t/remux
items.summary: The `remux` Rust project provides a self‑hosted media server with a Jellyfin‑compatible API for personal streaming.
items.detail: Implemented in Rust, `remux` offers a lightweight alternative to cloud‑based media services, exposing endpoints that Jellyfin clients can discover and use. The server handles transcoding, library indexing, and user authentication locally, giving users full control over their media without third‑party dependencies.

items.title: Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT
items.summary: OCCT is an open‑source C++ development platform supporting 3D CAD, CAM, and CAE applications.
items.detail: Open CASCADE Technology provides a comprehensive set of libraries for geometric modeling, visualization, and data exchange. Licensed under LGPL, it is used in both academic research and commercial engineering tools, offering extensible APIs for custom algorithm development.

items.title: The-Swarm-Corporation/AutoHedge
items.summary: AutoHedge is a GitHub project that lets you build an autonomous hedge fund in minutes using swarm intelligence and AI agents for market analysis, risk management, and trade execution.
items.detail: The tool combines multiple AI agents that each handle a specific trading function and coordinates them via a swarm‑based algorithm. It requires users to supply market data feeds and brokerage API keys, and it is not a regulated financial product. The repository includes example configurations to get started quickly.

items.title: Zie619/n8n-workflows
items.summary: Zie619/n8n-workflows is a GitHub collection of Python‑based n8n workflow definitions gathered from the official site and other sources.
items.detail: n8n is an open‑source workflow automation platform, and this repo aggregates community‑contributed workflow files for reuse. The collection is organized by category and includes JSON definitions that can be imported directly into an n8n instance. It serves as a quick‑start library for developers building automated pipelines.

items.title: apple/foundationdb
items.summary: apple/foundationdb hosts the open‑source, distributed, transactional key‑value store FoundationDB, written in C++ and maintained by Apple.
items.detail: FoundationDB provides strong ACID transactions across a horizontally scalable cluster and offers multiple language bindings. The project was open‑sourced by Apple in 2020 and continues to receive community contributions. It is used as a backend for services requiring reliable, multi‑model data storage.

items.title: argotorg/solidity
items.summary: argotorg/solidity mirrors the Solidity smart‑contract programming language source code, a C++ implementation used for Ethereum development.
items.detail: Solidity compiles high‑level contract code to Ethereum Virtual Machine bytecode and includes a standard library for common patterns. The repository contains the compiler, documentation, and test suites, enabling developers to build, test, and deploy contracts on Ethereum and compatible blockchains.
